Package edu.cnu.mdi.sim.demo.network

Class NetworkDeclutterSimulation

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.sim.demo.network.NetworkDeclutterSimulation
All Implemented Interfaces:
Simulation
public final class NetworkDeclutterSimulation extends Object implements Simulation
Force-directed "decluttering" simulation for a server/client network using normalized world coordinates.

The model lives in the unit square:

  • x in [0,1]
  • y in [0,1]

Rendering is responsible for mapping world coordinates into pixel coordinates. The view should also compute and populate NetworkModel.Node#worldRadius for each node every frame (or whenever the viewport size changes), so this simulation can:

  • apply overlap-aware repulsion based on icon size
  • clamp positions so icons remain fully visible inside the unit square

Force model

Each step computes the net force on each node as the sum of:

  1. Springs (edges) for each client→server connection: F = k * (r - r0) * rhat
    • r is current distance between endpoints
    • r0 is the equilibrium distance
    • k controls stiffness
  2. Repulsion (all pairs) for node separation: approximately F ~ repulsionC / (r^2 + eps) along rhat.

    Repulsion is increased if icons are close enough to overlap and may be further increased when one or both nodes are servers via serverRepulsion.

  3. Centering toward (0.5, 0.5): F = -centerK * (x - 0.5, y - 0.5).

    This prevents the common “everything evacuates to the boundary” artifact in layouts that combine repulsion with hard clamping. Set too high, it can also cause “all servers pile up in the center”, so keep it small.

Integration and convergence

Velocity is updated with damping: 

 v <- damping * v + dt * F
 x <- x + v

A per-component velocity clamp (vmax) limits occasional numeric spikes. The simulation stops when either:

  • cancel is requested,
  • the average node speed falls below settleVel() after minSteps, or
  • maxSteps is reached.

Parameter tuning hints (unit-square world)

  • Servers clump in the center: increase serverRepulsion, increase repulsionC, reduce centerK, or reduce k.
  • Clients collapse onto servers: increase r0 and/or repulsionC.
  • Layout “rings” the boundary: increase centerK slightly (but not too much) and/or reduce repulsionC.
  • Jitter/oscillation: increase damping, reduce k, reduce vmax.

    • cancel

      public void cancel(SimulationContext ctx)
      Cancellation hook called by the engine on the simulation thread.

      Posts a UI message and indeterminate progress indicator so the user sees immediate feedback. The engine calls Simulation.shutdown(SimulationContext) immediately after this method returns.

      No separate simulation-side cancellation flag is needed: SimulationContext.isCancelRequested() is the authoritative cancellation signal and is already checked at the top of step(SimulationContext).

      Specified by:
      cancel in interface Simulation
      Parameters:
      ctx - the simulation context

    • getDiagnosticsSamples

      public ConcurrentLinkedQueue<NetworkDeclutterSimulation.Diagnostics> getDiagnosticsSamples()
      Return the queue of per-step diagnostic samples produced during the simulation.

      The simulation enqueues a sample every 5 steps on the simulation thread. The view drains the queue by calling Queue.poll() repeatedly inside its onRefresh callback on the EDT. ConcurrentLinkedQueue is lock-free, so concurrent access from both threads is safe without any additional synchronization.

      Returns:
      the live diagnostics queue; never null

    • computeEnergy

      public NetworkDeclutterSimulation.Energy computeEnergy()
      Compute a pseudo-energy snapshot for the current layout.

      Delegates to computeEnergyInternal(), the single canonical implementation shared with computeDiagnostics(double, int, double) to eliminate code duplication.

      Note: These values are not a conserved Hamiltonian. See the class-level javadoc for the full explanation of the force/energy mismatch and other non-conservative effects.

      Returns:
      an NetworkDeclutterSimulation.Energy record for the current node positions and velocities

    • computeDiagnostics

      public NetworkDeclutterSimulation.Diagnostics computeDiagnostics(double avgSpeed, int vmaxHitCount, double FrmsNow)
      Compute a NetworkDeclutterSimulation.Diagnostics snapshot for the current model state.

      Energies are obtained from computeEnergyInternal() — the single canonical implementation shared with computeEnergy() — so the two can never diverge.

      The caller may supply avgSpeed and vmaxHitCount from values already computed during the integration step to avoid an extra O(N) scan. Pass Double.NaN / -1 to have this method recompute them from the current node velocities.

      Parameters:
      avgSpeed - mean node speed in world-units/step from the most recent integration, or Double.NaN to recompute
      vmaxHitCount - number of nodes that hit the speed clamp in the most recent integration step, or -1 to recompute
      FrmsNow - force RMS computed during the current step
      Returns:
      a fully-populated NetworkDeclutterSimulation.Diagnostics for the current step
